gaps.sentence: He ___ not understand the lecture at all yesterday.
gaps.hint: an inability that existed in the past
gaps.explanation: 'Could not' expresses past inability: could not understand.

gaps.sentence: When the lift broke, I ___ walk up ten flights of stairs.
gaps.hint: necessity created by a past event
gaps.explanation: 'Had to' expresses past necessity: had to walk.

gaps.sentence: You ___ bring your own laptop — we will provide everything.
gaps.hint: no obligation, so needn't not mustn't
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' means it is not necessary; 'mustn't' would mean it is prohibited: needn't bring.

gaps.sentence: Luckily I ___ find a parking space right outside the theatre.
gaps.hint: one particular success on that occasion
gaps.explanation: One particular success takes 'was able to': was able to find.

gaps.sentence: Need we ___ the whole report, or just the summary?
gaps.hint: modal need takes the bare infinitive
gaps.explanation: When 'need' is a modal in questions and negatives, it takes the bare infinitive: read.

gaps.sentence: Nobody ___ have predicted that result — it shocked everyone.
gaps.hint: it was impossible at that time
gaps.explanation: 'Could have' in negatives means it was not possible: could have predicted.

gaps.sentence: There ___ be a mistake — I ordered the vegetarian option.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' expresses the speaker's certainty about a present situation: must be.

gaps.sentence: They ___ have checked the dates before booking — now they have lost the money.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have' expresses criticism of something not done: should have.
